messages:
tara (Product): Heads-up 1: competitor FastEmbed announced a sub-10ms 1536-dim dense embedding offering with a blowout cost number. Customers pinging us asking why we don't match. Link: https://fastembed.example/blog/low-latency :loud_sound:

raj (Research): saw that. they claim quantized ops + AVX512 kernels on CPU + a proprietary caching layer. claim looks like a strong engineering hack rather than model change.

miguel (Eng-ML): quick bench skepticism: 10ms for 1536-d dim at p99 seems plausible if model small + on-nic cache. but quality tradeoffs unknown. we need to validate embedding cosine variance vs our base models.

samir (Sales): commercial impact: two pilot prospects mentioned FastEmbed as "baseline" now. we need a comms plan. Either match latency or own the quality narrative.

hannah (Growth): marketing angle: if we can't match raw latency without cost spike, lean into "quality per token" and "predictable latency at scale". but customers care about client-perceived latency.

oliver (Customer Success): field notes: two SMBs asked for "embeddings under 20ms" to speed up their search UI. They said they'd consider switching if latency helps UX. Not all customers can accept lower quality.

miguel (Eng-ML): propose options: A) parity play: optimize our embedding runtime (quantization + batching) to target 15-20ms p95 on hosted for 1536-dim; B) differentiator: ship a latency-aware serving tier with SLA and token-aware batching that keeps quality high; C) hybrid: offer "fast" low-cost quantized variant plus clear eval dashboard.

raj (Research): cost/quality data we need: 1) embedding quality drop vs anchor (recall@k on common evals), 2) p95/p99 latency at different loads, 3) unit cost delta. I can run eval suites if Miguel provides quantized checkpoints.

tara (Product): suggested MLP to respond: 1) do an outreach benchmark vs FastEmbed on 3 representative corpora (search, recommendations, legal QA) in 10 days, 2) prototype a "fast-embed" runtime knob with config and docs, 3) customer-facing comparison doc + runbook for pilot. Goal: show pilot path in 3 weeks.

samir (Sales): 3 weeks is tight but doable for pilot LOIs. I'll surface this in deals. Need a one-pager we can share ASAP.

miguel (Eng-ML): I'll prioritize a 7-day spike: - build quantized pipeline (8-bit) for our 1536 model - measure recall@10 and cosine drift - bench p95/p99 at 100rps and 500rps.

raj (Research): I'll run cross-corpus evals once Miguel has artifacts. ETA for initial numbers: 9 working days.

hannah (Growth): I'll draft a neutral comparison one-pager that emphasizes tradeoffs (latency vs quality vs cost) and suggested UI hints for teams to mitigate.

oliver (Customer Success): I'll collect concrete customer latency targets and prioritize top 5 accounts to invite to pilot.

ops-bot: scheduled: embed-quant-spike job started by miguel at 2155000008

tara (Product): decision pathway: if quality drop <=5% recall and latency gain >2x, we consider shipping a fast-tier. If quality loss >10%, promote a differentiated messaging play + optimize batching for medium latency wins. Reconvene in 11 days with data. :eyes:
